newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN to screen Rwandan ex-soldiers in Central Africa.
newsitem.headline: UN to screen Rwandan ex-soldiers in Central Africa.

text.p: Hundreds of members of Rwanda's former Hutu government army who have fled to the Central African Republic from Zaire may lose their refugee status after being screened by the U.N. refugee agency, a UNHCR spokesman said on Tuesday.
Fernando del Mundo said the UNHCR planned to send a protection team to the country soon for status determination for a group of 800 Rwandan Hutu refugees who had fled there in recent weeks.
Nearly two-thirds were male and former soldiers of Rwanda. Most had surrendered their weapons, he said.
"Most of these people are male and ex-military. If these people are found out to be former soldiers or militiamen, then they will lose their refugee status," the spokesman said.
The 1951 U.N. convention on refugees stipulates that people who have committed war crimes or crimes against humanity should be excluded from refugee status.

Former soldiers of Rwanda's ex-government Hutu army and militiamen played a key role in 1994's slaughter of half a million minority Tutsis and Hutu moderates and fled to Zaire with two million Hutu refugees in fear of retribution.

Human rights groups have criticised the UNHCR for treating killers as refugees in thriving camps in eastern Zaire which the agency administered before they were emptied by Tutsi-dominated rebels late last year.

The agency says the international community never gave the assistance it needed to separate militiamen from ordinary refugees at camps within striking distance of Rwanda, which were used as staging posts for cross-border rebel attacks.

Aid officials in Geneva said the International Committee of the Red Cross may take charge of looking after the former Hutu soldiers in Central African Republic depending on the outcome of UNHCR's status determination.
ICRC spokesman Rolin Wavre said his Swiss-run agency was discussing the matter with the UNHCR but declined to give details.
